title: Wandering in the CKS Memorial Hall
store: CKS Memorial Hall Museum Gift Shop
description: Pastel painting capturing the grand architecture of the National Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall with its blue octogonal roof, white marble walls and tiered base, viewed from the surrounding gardens with a lotus pond framing the foreground. Titled "Early Summer at Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall" (初夏的中正紀念堂) by the Taiwanese artist Chang Zhe-xiong (張哲雄).
history: Following the death of President Chiang Kai-shek in 1975, architect Yang Cho-cheng designed this landmark which opened to the public on April 5, 1980. Over the decades, its massive front courtyard—now called Liberty Square—has evolved from an authoritarian monument into the vibrant epicenter of Taiwan's modern democratic gatherings and civil protests. The artwork depicted in the postcard is preserved in the Taiwan Cultural Memory Bank.
note: The back says: 'Spreading the Fragrance of Flowers and Plants, Enriching the Growth of Heaven and Earth. Each encounter weaves together moments of tenderness and longing, one by one'. To my disappointment, it was raining the day I visited and seeing how goergous the colours look during the summer, I made a promise to myself that I would come back to chase the sunnier weather.

title: Snack Price List
store: 來好 LAI HAO 凱撒二店
description: Vintage Taiwanese advertisement features six panels arranged in a grid, showcasing retro summer refreshments. The top row displays a green glass bottle of HeySong Soda, a classic bottle of Coca-Cola on ice, and a colorful tin of grape juice. The bottom row includes a paper cup of ice cream, a packaged chocolate ice pop, and simple green and pink popsicles, accompanied by vertical Chinese text and historical prices
history: This menu illustrates the mid-20th-century consumer landscape in Taiwan, where local staples met expanding Western influences. Homegrown brands represented deep-rooted tradition, while the presence of Coca-Cola highlights the post-war arrival of multinational corporations. The shift toward mass-produced ice cream cups and wrapped popsicles reflects the rise of commercial refrigeration and a booming modern snack culture.
note: Tawainese food might be one of my favourite cusines, and there is something so conforming in retro branding designs. so colourful and honest.

title: Potasse d'Alsace
description: Oval-shaped vintage ad with a royal blue background and bold white text at the bottom reading "POTASSE D'ALSACE". In the center, a white stork with a black wing and red legs stands on one foot. The lower background features a black silhouette of a city skyline, with the sharp spire of a gothic cathedral.
history: This iconic artwork was designed in 1929 by the famous Alsacian illustrator Hansi, as a marketing campaign for the regional potassium mines. It was widely distributed across Europe and North America as promotional postcards, posters, and enamel signs to market Alsacian potash as a premium agricultural fertilizer. Today, the imagery is highly celebrated both as a symbol of Alsacian cultural heritage and as a valuable collector's item in vintage advertising.

title: Straatsoper, Wien
description: Solid black background with the word "WIEN" written across the bottom half in large, elongated, orange-brown block letters. The top half showcases a circular illustration of the grand, illuminated facade of the Vienna State Opera house. In front of the building, a bustling crowd is artistically represented by a vibrant mosaic of hundreds of small, multicolored dots that simulate late-19th to early-20th-century formal attire.
history: This image belongs to the highly sought-after artistic postcards produced during the Vienna Secession and Wiener Werkstätte movements around 1900–1910. Graphic designers and artists of this era created these cards to democratize modern art, transforming everyday tourist souvenirs into collectible, high-design masterpieces. The styling perfectly captures the affluent, avant-garde Fin de Siècle atmosphere of Vienna's golden cultural age.
note: My prized possession, I find this postcard so creatively charming for no reason, I spent no more than 2 hours in the city the first time I visited Vienna and 20 minutes were spent exploring the store I bought this at. I haven't been able to find who made it, but I will.

title: Pastel de nata
store: IPOR Livraria Portuguesa e Galeria de Arte
description: Detailed color drawing of four Portuguese egg tarts (pastéis de nata) clustered tightly together. The tarts have a golden, flaky puff pastry crust and custard centers featuring distinct dark, caramelized blisters. On the left side of the tarts, the Portuguese words "Pastel de nata" are written in an elegant, handwritten cursive font, accompanied vertically by bold Chinese characters reading "澳門葡萄撻" (Macau Portuguese Tart)
history: The Portuguese egg tart is a defining culinary symbol of Macau's unique, centuries-old Sino-Portuguese fusion culture. Originally inspired by traditional conventual sweets from Lisbon monasteries, the recipe was modified locally in Macau during the late 20th century to create a distinctly creamier, less sweet version. Today, this globally famous pastry represents how colonial heritage seamlessly blended with Cantonese preferences, making it a proud icon of Macau's identity and street food scene.
note: Pastéis de nata taste diferent around the world, macanese egg tarts are not as sweet and obvisouly i'm a little biased towards the originals, but how fun to travel to the other side of the world and get to have a piece of home with you.

title: Ginja de Portugal
description: Vintage pale-green Portuguese liquor label featuring a diagonal white banner with bold red letters reading "GINJA DE PORTUGAL." A branch of vibrant red sour cherries drops over a pink ribbon marked "LICOR SUPERFINO," next to two gold medals and the royal coat of arms. The bottom displays an illustration of Lisbon's historic Belém Tower on the water, alongside a pink circular stamp showing a red anchor for "FABRICA ANCORA."
history: Fábrica Âncora, an iconic Lisbon distillery founded in 1882 that eventually became the official supplier to the Portuguese royal family. Ginjinha is a beloved traditional sour cherry liqueur that stands as Lisbon's most iconic regional drink. By pairing the historic Belém Tower with international gold medals, the label reflects the national pride and global ambitions of 19th-century Portuguese craftsmanship.
note: Bought at one of my favourite places in lisbon that no longer exists.

title: Evzones
description: Group of four Greek soldiers (Evzones) marching in perfect synchronization across a paved stone courtyard. They are dressed in their historic ceremonial military uniforms, featuring white plisséd skirts, long stockings, and hats with hanging black tassels. In the background, Greek text is engraved directly into the large cream-colored stone blocks of the monument wall.
history: The Evzones (or Tsoliades) are part of the elite Presidential Guard unit of the Greek Army. Founded officially in 1868 as a crack light infantry unit, they served with great distinction in major conflicts like the Balkan Wars and World War I. Today, their role is purely ceremonial, but they remain powerful symbols of national pride, military valor, and historical struggle. Published by Editions Sotiris Toumbis.
note: I find the composition of this quite intriguing it's unusual, a little off since every subject is turned away from the viewers perpective. It reminds me of something out of a photography book.

title: Edelweiss
description: Vintage-style botanical illustration featuring several white edelweiss flowers with velvety petals and yellow centers in the foreground. In the background, a majestic, snow-dusted alpine mountain peak rises against a muted, earthy-toned sky. The bottom of the artwork includes elegant cursive script and French text identifying the scenic location.
history: Edelweiss is a deeply cherished emblem of Swiss and Austrian national identity, frequently used by elite alpine military units to represent rugged resilience. Its immense popularity during the 19th-century alpine tourism boom led to over-picking, making it one of the first plants in the world to be legally protected. The postcard artwork is by Catherine Ernst, a contemporary Swiss botanical illustrator and painter known for her detailed depictions of alpine flora.ns.
note: My first postcard ever! from a free weekend when i was interning in Meyrin at 18 years old, what a time. If only she knew it would be the first of many. in a way I'm sure she did,

title: Future
description: Colorful, highly detailed contemporary tapestry featuring two men standing side-by-side in white and light pink suits overlayed with molecular and abstract line drawings. They are surrounded by an intricate background packed with psychedelic patterns, scientific diagrams, circuitry motifs, and royal coats of arms in the four corners.
history: Titled "Fremtiden" (The Future), this piece is part of a series of 17 modern tapestries designed by Danish artist Bjørn Nørgaard and woven by Manufacture des Gobelins as a 50th birthday gift for Queen Margrethe II of Denmark. It hangs in Christiansborg Palace and depicts her two sons—the current King Frederik X and Prince Joachim—surrounded by technological and biological motifs to symbolize the future of the nation and its monarchy.
note: Absolutely loved the tapestries, this one was my favourite. Maybe because it looks towards the future rather than depict past events. Not a postcard but a greeting card, but I couldn't not bring a bit of the art with me.

title: Injured Bridge
description: Folk-art style painting depicts a winter cityscape featuring a massive terracota archway and a right-side cliffside dripping with red, blood-like streaks. Tiny stylized figures walk across the snowy ground and winding paths amidst bare trees, with red-roofed buildings and distant twin cathedral spires lining the horizon.
history: Painted in 1941 by Czech artist Karel Otto Hrubý during the Nazi occupation of Czechoslovakia, this artwork is titled "Krvácující most" (The Injured Bridge). The surreal imagery of blood pouring from the city's structures serves as a powerful wartime allegory for the violence, suffering, and political oppression experienced by the population.
note: One of my personal favourites, I find disturbing imagery fascinating and it made me wonder what surreal representation of a more dark event this could be, as I was oblivious of its history at the time.

title: Tokei (Tokyo): Hiroo and Roppongi
description: Bird's-eye-view illustration shows a modern Tokyo cityscape featuring the Roppongi Hills tower surrounded by dense urban housing. Floating, scalloped golden clouds slice through the landscape, creating a stark contrast against the muted greys and whites of the buildings.
history: Created by contemporary artist Akira Yamaguchi, this artwork utilizes the traditional Yamato-e and Ukiyo-e styles to comment on Japan's rapid post-war modernization. By superimposing historical artistic conventions—like golden mist and bird's-eye perspective—onto 21st-century infrastructure, it explores the tension between cultural heritage and urban development. The inclusion of samurai-era architecture alongside modern skyscrapers highlights the layers of history coexisting within modern Tokyo.

title: My Neighbour Totoro
description: Soft watercolor illustration by Hayao Miyazaki showing the character Mei in winter clothes looking up at a large Totoro covered in snow, with the Japanese text わたしはだれだ…？ (Who am I...?) written below.
history: Created during the early concept stages of the 1988 Studio Ghibli masterpiece My Neighbor Totoro, this artwork reflects Miyazaki's unique pre-production design process and soft artistic style. Over the decades, it has become a beloved piece of Ghibli merchandise, appearing on official seasonal stationery and packaging for the famous Shiro-Hige's Totoro Cream Puff Shop in Tokyo.

title: A Pint of Sheep
description: Graphic illustration of a stylized pint glass filled with curly-textured black sheep representing the dark stout beer, topped with a thick head of white-wooled sheep acting as the foam, all set against a black background with the title "A Pint of Sheep" at the top.
history: Created as a popular contemporary Irish souvenir design, this artwork playfully combines two of Ireland's most famous cultural icons: its rural abundance of sheep and its world-renowned dark stout beer (Guinness). It serves as a humorous visual pun tailored for the tourism market, celebrating Irish identity and wit through a clever pop-art graphic.

title: Jety-Oguz 'Seven Oxen'
description: Photograph of the Jety-Oguz rock formation in Kyrgyzstan under a bright, cloudy blue sky. A massive row of jagged red sandstone cliffs dominates the background, stretching across the frame. The foreground shows a green valley filled with tall pine trees, a traditional white yurt, and a couple of small houses.
history: Named "Seven Oxes" in Kyrgyz, these rocks are tied to an ancient legend of seven bulls turned to stone by the gods to stop a tragic bloodshed. Historically, this scenic valley served as a notable passage along the Silk Road for traders crossing the Tian Shan mountains. Today, it stands as a prominent symbol of Kyrgyz national identity and traditional nomadic heritage.

title: Date Night
description: A surreal corner room with vibrant red walls where a large, pink-skinned arm reaches from the right to lift a businessman in a blue suit with chopsticks. In the foreground, a giant black bowl is filled with yellow ramen noodles and a hard-boiled egg next to a small green bowl holding a pair of legs and a red rose, while a third figure falls upside down onto the noodles beneath a small yellow fire emblem on the wall.
history: Created in 2021 by the contemporary Indian artist and creative director Sargam Gupta, this artwork belongs to a series exploring themes of modern romance, routine, and emotional surrealism. The visual metaphor flips the dynamics of a typical dinner setting into an existential playground, using bold pop-art textures, high-contrast primary colors, and playful distortions to comment on the consumerist nature and overwhelming sensory experiences of contemporary human dating and relationships.

title: Map of Fushimi Inari
description: Colorful, hand-drawn map of the Fushimi Inari-taisha shrine complex set against a bright yellow background. It depicts mountain trails densely packed with traditional architecture, waterfalls, cartoon white foxes, and paths lined with vibrant orange torii gates. Major landmarks and intersections are clearly marked with rectangular labels in both Japanese kanji and English.
history: Founded in 711 AD, Fushimi Inari-taisha is the head Shinto shrine dedicated to Inari, the deity of rice, agriculture, and business prosperity. The thousands of iconic orange torii gates lining the mountain paths were donated by businesses and individuals seeking financial good fortune. This specific illustrated map is a popular tourist navigation guide distributed locally in Kyoto to help visitors hike the sacred trail.

title: Ding Ding Tram
description: Watercolor painting of a bustling city street featuring two iconic double-decker trams traveling along metal tracks. The tram on the left is a vibrant solid yellow, while the tram on the right is white with a distinct red upper deck showing passengers visible through the top windows. Pedestrians wait on the sidewalk to the right, yellow public buses are parked in the background, and a prominent green traffic light stands in the lower-left foreground.
history: This piece belongs to a series of urban landscapes by renowned watercolor master Shen Ping, a permanently settled Hong Kong artist known for capturing local culture, busy harbors, and street life. The artwork depicts Hong Kong's famous double-decker trams, affectionately known locally as "Ding Ding," which have been operating on Hong Kong Island since 1904. As the world's largest double-decker tram fleet still in service, the transit line functions as a living cultural symbol of the city's urban heritage. Ping's signature unrestrained brushstrokes beautifully document the nostalgic charm of these traditional vehicles navigating the fast-paced, modern development of Hong Kong.

title: Utopies Bruxelloises
description: This artwork depicts a dense, futuristic metropolis rising directly behind traditional European-style houses with red-tiled roofs. High-overhead elevated highways and multi-tiered skyways cross between soaring, pale golden skyscrapers and sphere-like structures, while sleek aircraft zoom through a warm, reddish-orange sky.
history: This illustration is by renowned French artist François Schuiten, taken from his acclaimed graphic novel series Les Cités Obscures (The Obscure Cities) created with writer Benoît Peeters. The image draws heavy inspiration from Retro-Futurism and 19th-century architecture, particularly reflecting the historical concept of "Brusselization"—the rapid, controversial introduction of modern high-rises into historic urban areas in post-WWII Brussels.

title: Naval Flag of the Chinese Republic
store: 來好 LAI HAO 凱撒二店
description: Vintage printed illustration of a flag waving on a silver pole with a golden finial, set against a plain, off-white background. The flag features a vibrant red field with a dark blue canton in the upper-left corner, which contains a sharp white sun with 12 rays. Printed text at the bottom left reads "102. The Naval Flag of the Chinese Republic," while the corresponding traditional Chinese characters (中華民國海軍旗) appear at the bottom right.
history: The image illustrates the national flag of the Republic of China (ROC), historically designated in early 20th-century military charts as the naval jack or naval flag before becoming the official national flag in 1928. Designed by Sun Yat-sen and Lu Haodong, the colors represent the Three Principles of the People: blue for nationalism and liberty, white for democracy and equality, and red for livelihood and fraternity, with the 12 rays symbolizing the hours of the day and months of the year. This specific document is a historical print or postcard from the Republican era used to document and publicize the state symbols of the newly established republic to domestic and international audiences.

title: Then the Tabby went far, and farther than far
description: monochrome, vintage-style pencil and charcoal illustration depicting a large, wide-eyed tabby cat walking forward along a dirt pathway. The cat's body is hunched forward in an intense, menacing posture, with its tail raised high and its mouth open to expose sharp, prominent teeth. It features prominent dark stripes across its fur and ears drawn back, emerging from a softly rendered, textured background of forest foliage and trees.
history: This artwork is a famous 1906 drawing titled "Så gikk kjetta langt og lenger enn langt" ("Then the Tabby went far, and farther than far") by the celebrated Norwegian artist Theodor Kittelsen. It was created as a folklore illustration for the popular Norwegian fairy tale "The Tabby who was such a Glutton" (Kjetta som var saa gammel til å ete), published in collections by Peter Christen Asbjørnsen and Jørgen Moe. Kittelsen is highly regarded in Norway for his atmospheric and sometimes unsettling depictions of nature, fairy tales, and mythical trolls.
note: I like to image the cat gets bigger every step it takes.

title: Constantinople, the Top-Kahné Mosque
description: Oil painting capturing a serene waterfront scene bathed in glowing, atmospheric blue and gold light at dusk or dawn. In the foreground, figures navigate a small wooden rowboat across softly rippling waters toward a grand mosque featuring a central dome, illuminated arches, and two towering minarets along the shoreline.
history: This artwork is by the Russian-Armenian Romantic painter Ivan Aivazovsky, celebrated for his dramatic atmospheric vistas and marine landscapes. The scene depicts 19th-century Constantinople (present-day Istanbul) along the Bosporus, capturing the city's iconic Ottoman architecture through the European Orientalist fascination with the beauty and light of the East.

title: L'Alsace Enchantée
description: This watercolor painting by Georges Ratkoff depicts a nostalgic, snow-covered street corner in Colmar, France, featuring traditional warm-toned half-timbered houses with steep, white-blanketed roofs. In the foreground, 19th-century pedestrians and a horse-drawn carriage pass a glowing street lamp and an arched storefront labeled "Cellier du Koïfhus."
history: The artwork illustrates the historical charm of Colmar in the Alsace region, specifically referencing the Koïfhus (Old Custom House), a 15th-century hub of regional trade. The creator, French artist Georges Ratkoff, spent decades capturing these idyllic, folkloric winter landscapes to celebrate and preserve traditional Alsatian culture.

title: Suite de Fados
description: This is the illustrated cover of a vintage sheet music booklet set against a vibrant yellow background, created by modernist artist Stuart de Carvalhais (signed as STVAR on the left). The central drawing shows a man in a green jacket and flat cap sitting on a red wooden stool playing a Portuguese guitar, while a woman draped in a traditional black shawl leans over his shoulder. The stylized typography at the top reads "Suite de Fados" and "One Step," with the composer's name, Silva Negrão, written in the center and the [Sassetti & C.ª Editores] logo at the bottom.
history: This cover was designed in the early 20th century for a piano arrangement by maestro Silva Negrão, published by the prominent Lisbon house [Sassetti]. The piece reflects a unique cultural crossover of the 1910s and 1920s, merging the soulful melodies of Portuguese fado with the upbeat rhythm of the American one-step dance craze sweeping Europe. The illustrator, [Stuart de Carvalhais], was a pioneering Portuguese caricaturist, and his iconic imagery here remains an enduring visual symbol of classic Lisbon fado culture.

title: Church of Our Lady of Remedy
description: This is a vibrant watercolor painting depicting a panoramic view of a coastal town, with the handwritten word "Kotor" in the top right corner. The right foreground features a prominent white church bell tower with a domed roof and cross, surrounded by orange-roofed houses and lush green trees. In the background, a bright blue bay stretches toward towering mountains painted in shades of blue and purple under a clear sky.
history: The artwork depicts the historic town of Kotor in Montenegro, famous for its well-preserved medieval old town and its UNESCO-protected bay. The tower represents the Church of Our Lady of Remedy, built in 1518 on the mountain slopes by plague survivors, making it a landmark along the steep path to Saint John's Fortress. This contemporary urban watercolor sketch beautifully captures the dramatic natural landscape where the rugged Balkan mountains meet the Adriatic Sea.

title: Oil painting of Prala de Ferreira do Amaral, Macao
store: IPOR Livraria Portuguesa e Galeria de Arte
description: Impasto oil painting by Ada Zhang capturing the Macau skyline under a soft blue sky. The center is dominated by the golden, towering Grand Lisboa hotel with its distinctive lotus-flower shape, flanked on the left by a dark purple skyscraper illuminated by yellow window lights. The foreground features a sweeping road and roundabout rendered with thick, expressive brushstrokes of purple, grey, and brown paint.
history: The artwork depicts Ferreira do Amaral Square in Macau, with the background showcasing the iconic Grand Lisboa casino-hotel opened in 2007. The building's unique design honors the lotus flower, the official floral emblem of Macau since its sovereignty transfer from Portugal to China in 1999. Contemporary artist Ada Zhang (張洪) utilizes a heavy oil texture to document the high-energy urban dynamism and opulence defining modern Macau.

title: Kitten mascot of the aircraft carrier HMS Eagle
description: Black-and-white photograph shows a small, striped tabby cat resting comfortably in a miniature, custom-made canvas hammock complete with tiny pillows. The hammock is suspended indoors against a metallic, industrial backdrop, featuring a large oval hatch or bulkhead door in the background
history: This famous photograph from the Imperial War Museum archives captures "Unsinkable Sam" (or similar ship's mascot, famously known as Convoy, the ship's cat aboard HMS Hermes in 1941). Ships' cats were a longstanding naval tradition across military and merchant vessels, kept both for practical pest control and as beloved mascots to boost crew morale during World War II.

title: Taipei Chifeng Street Alleyway
description: Watercolor-and-ink illustration of a narrow alley between tall, weathered apartment buildings under a bright blue sky. An orange awning shades a shopfront on the left, a streetlamp arches over the lane on the right, and bicycles and scooters line the street. Yellow crisscross lines are painted on the foreground pavement.
history: Chifeng Street in Taipei's Datong District is an older neighborhood known for its narrow lanes, workshops, and local shops, and in recent years it has also become a hub for cafés and creative businesses. The illustration captures that balance between traditional daily life and urban renewal, a common theme in the "urban sketching" movement.

title: Viennese specialities
description: Hand-colored promotional illustration featuring classic Austrian treats against a textured pink background with a yellow border. The top showcases an "Einspänner" coffee in a tall glass topped with whipped cream, the middle displays a "Melange" coffee served on a silver tray with water and sugar cubes, and the bottom highlights a slice of "Sachertorte" chocolate cake complete with whipped cream and a small fork.
history: Artwork was created by Martina Nieß as part of the official "Vienna is different" (Wien ist anders) marketing campaign, a long-running promotional initiative designed to highlight the capital's unique charm, humor, and cultural quirks. The piece celebrates Vienna's UNESCO-recognized coffeehouse culture, featuring the driver-historied Einspänner, the classic Melange, and the famous Sachertorte invented in 1832. Through its approachable graphic style, the illustration effectively uses traditional culinary staples to capture the distinct, welcoming lifestyle that sets Vienna apart for international travelers.

title: Amsterdam
description: vibrant, cartoon-style postcard illustration of Amsterdam set against a bustling canal backdrop with clear blue skies. The scene showcases rows of traditional Dutch canal houses with distinctive stepped, spout, and neck gables, while a crowded arched bridge spans across the water. The canals and streets are packed to the brim with humorous details, including numerous tour boats, a capsizing vessel, chaotic crowds, and a mouse floating away on an orange balloon in the top-left corner.
history: The artwork is a highly detailed, comical illustration by renowned Dutch cartoonist Frans Le Roux, widely celebrated for his chaotic cityscapes created for puzzles and postcards. The piece captures the architectural spirit of Amsterdam's Canal Ring, a UNESCO World Heritage site built primarily during the Dutch Golden Age in the 17th century. Through its lively and satirical style, the illustration playfully caricatures the city's frantic tourist culture, busy water traffic, and historic charm, making it a popular memento for visitors.

title: JOB
description: An Art Nouveau poster of a woman with long, dark, flowing hair adorned with red flowers, reclining in a pale orange-yellow gown. She holds a lit cigarette in one raised hand and a small JOB packet in the other. A large green circle frames her, with big brown "JOB" lettering across the top and a yellow geometric pattern behind.
history: Designed by Czech artist Alphonse Mucha in 1898, this lithograph was a commercial advertisement for the French JOB cigarette paper company [JOB Collection]. It defines the Art Nouveau movement's trend of blending fine art with mass advertising to sell products through stylized, sensory imagery. The woman's cascading, swirling hair became a hallmark of the Belle Époque design aesthetic.

title: The Smile of the Alberta Sphinx
description: Whimsical illustration of two large white lion statues perched on the rooftop of an ornate stone building against a starry night sky. Between them stands a girl in a bright pink dress, reaching toward one of the lions, with a small tabby cat sitting on the ledge below and a few tiny colorful creatures nearby. A sculpted face relief decorates the building's facade.
history: This illustration by Latvian artist Anita Paegle is titled The Smile of the Alberta Sphinx ("Sfinksas Albertas smaids"). Created with delicate watercolors, the artwork reimagines the iconic Art Nouveau (Jūgendstils) architectural heritage of Riga, Latvia, transforming the real-world stone lions and expressive facade sculptures found on historic Alberta Street into whimsical characters under a starry night sky.

title: Bondegård
description: A vibrant, cartoonish farm landscape set against a rich teal backdrop with thick, bold black outlines. A cheerful mix of animals—including a blue dog, pink pigs, a smiling horse, red cows, and white sheep—surround two white houses with bright red roofs flying a Danish flag.
history: Created by celebrated Danish artist Bo Bendixen (studio founded in 1973), this piece exemplifies modern Scandinavian graphic design. Known for his joyful optimism and minimalist forms, Bendixen captures the idealized Danish countryside (det danske landskab). His iconic style combines pop-art simplicity with Nordic motifs, making his posters a staple of late 20th-century Danish culture and home decor.

title: Tarde de Castanha, Noz e Alfarroba
description: Hand-drawn infographic postcard provides a visual recipe for an autumn chestnut, walnut, and carob tart, featuring minimalist watercolor sketches of measuring cups, whole nuts, dried figs, and preparation steps alongside clear, handwritten Portuguese text.
history: Created by the Portuguese ecological art project Criatividade ao Lume, the piece highlights traditional regional ingredients like carob (alfarroba) and chestnuts (castanhas), which carry deep seasonal significance in Portugal's autumn culinary heritage and harvest celebrations. 2 cups of flour, 1 cup of carob flour, 4 tablespoons of olive oil, 2 tablespoons of water, 8 walnuts, and 8 boiled chestnuts until a uniform dough forms, then press it into a pan and bake at 180°C (350°F) for 15 minutes. Next, make the filling by dissolving 1/2 cup of corn flour into 2 and 1/2 cups of water in a pot, cooking it over low heat while stirring continuously, and allowing it to boil for 1 to 2 minutes before turning off the flame. Finally, transfer this cooked mixture to a blender along with 12 walnuts and 4 dried figs, blend until it becomes a completely smooth cream, and pour it into the baked crust to cool and set completely before serving.

title: Le Petit Prince
description: Minimalist illustration on a postcard depicts The Little Prince with his iconic blonde hair and green suit sitting thoughtfully on a red airplane atop a small asteroid, surrounded by stars and a fox under the French quote, "Pour les uns, qui voyagent, les étoiles sont des guides" ("For some who travel, the stars are guides").
history: Written and illustrated by French aviator Antoine de Saint-Exupéry in 1943 during WWII, this whimsical philosophical fable has become one of the most translated and culturally cherished books in history. The image captures the story's core themes of profound isolation, wonder, and the searching nature of human connection.

title: Festas de Lisboa '24
description: Minimalist graphic poster featuring a vibrant electric yellow background. The center contains a high-contrast magenta image of a potted bush basil plant (manjerico) with a tiny, rectangular paper flag tucked into its leaves. The top left corner displays a circular "LISBOA CULTURA" logo, and the bottom features the bold, black text "FESTAS DE LISBOA '24."
history: Official promotional poster for the 2024 Festas de Lisboa, a month-long midsummer festival held every June in Portugal's capital. The featured manjerico plant is the ultimate cultural symbol of the city's St. Anthony celebrations, traditionally gifted to loved ones along with a small paper flag containing a romantic, poetic verse. Commissioned by Lisbon's municipal cultural department, the modern design represents the city's blend of contemporary identity with historic traditions like street parties (arraiais) and neighborhood parades.

title: The land of the midnight sun
description: Illustrated, colorful map of Norway set against a white background, filled with playful drawings of landmarks and wildlife. The cursive title "The land of the midnight sun" sits in the top-left corner, while "Norway" is written in large text at the bottom right. The map features polar bears in the north, an elk in the center, and whales in the surrounding blue ocean. Major cities like Oslo, Bergen, and Trondheim are marked with sketches of historic buildings, alongside a small block of handwritten factual data about the country.
history: This piece is a classic mid-to-late 20th-century souvenir postcard designed for the Norwegian tourism boom. It highlights core pillars of Norway's national identity: its rich Viking heritage, its modern maritime economy (symbolized by the offshore oil rig), and its breathtaking Arctic geography. The famous moniker "The Land of the Midnight Sun" celebrates the unique natural phenomenon occurring north of the Arctic Circle during summer, which remains a primary global attraction for travelers.

title: Blades from Momoyogusa
description: A traditional Japanese woodblock print composed of diagonal, overlapping rectangular strips overlaid on a tan textured background. Each strip contains stylized figures rendered with black line work, flat colors like green, yellow, and black, and expressive facial features characteristic of classical Japanese illustration. In the upper right corner, a small, circular red artist's seal is stamped onto the background.
history: This image is a woodblock print by the renowned Japanese artist Kamisaka Sekka (1866-1942) from his famous multi-volume masterwork Momoyogusa (Flowers of a Hundred Worlds), published in 1909. Sekka was the leading figure of the early 20th-century revival of the Rinpa school, an artistic style that emphasized stylized natural motifs, literature-inspired subjects, and innovative graphic layouts. This specific composition uses a distinct narrative framing technique reminiscent of traditional emaki (handscrolls), creating a dynamic visual rhythm that bridges traditional Edo-period aesthetics with early modern design.

title: Children of the Forest
description: A whimsical watercolor illustration depicting a family of miniature forest children harvesting wild goods in a lush green clearing. The children are dressed in simple light tunics, and most wear bright red hats with white spots resembling amanita mushrooms. One woman in a white dress carries a large basket overflowing with red berries, while small children carry enormous mushrooms—including a bright yellow chanterelle. In the background, a figure with a pinecone head works with a small axe near towering, realistic wild mushrooms and green moss.
history: This image is a classic illustration by the famous Swedish author and illustrator Elsa Beskow (1874–1953), taken from her beloved 1910 children's book Tomtebobarnen (Children of the Forest). Beskow is a cornerstone of Nordic children's literature, renowned for her ability to weave contemporary Art Nouveau styling with traditional Swedish folklore. Her work deeply reflects the Scandinavian cultural love for nature and the countryside, reimagining the forest floor as a magical, harmonious community. Postcards featuring her artwork have been widely collected across Europe for over a century, celebrating nostalgic, idyllic themes of childhood and the changing seasons.

title: Saint-Nicolas à Colmar
description: Detailed, vintage-style illustration depicts Saint Nicholas walking through a snow-covered street in Colmar, France, accompanied by a donkey carrying treats, while children gather around him and a local butcher offers provisions beneath elaborate, traditional wrought-iron shop signs at night.
history: Created in 1938 by the famous Alsatian artist and satirist Hansi (Jean-Jacques Waltz), the artwork reflects the deep cultural importance of Saint Nicholas Day celebrations in northeastern France and the region's distinct architectural heritage. The piece serves as a poignant, idealized celebration of Alsatian identity and traditions, produced during a tense historical period just before the outbreak of World War II.

title: Hong Kong Inspired Elements
description: Colorful watercolor collage of Hong Kong cultural icons on a white background with faint yellow dots. It features detailed drawings of local street foods like egg tarts, traditional transport like a green tram and red taxi, and landmarks like the Clock Tower. The text includes a prominent "Hong Kong" label in a plaid frame and small Chinese captions.
history: The postcard highlights Hong Kong's unique blend of British colonial history and Cantonese traditions, centered around its famous Cha Chaan Teng (local café) culture. Historic transit systems like the Star Ferry and "Ding Ding" tram have kept the city connected since the late 19th century. The featured comfort foods reflect a distinct culinary identity created by adapting Western snacks to local tastes after World War II.

title: Bauta
description: Detailed watercolor illustration of an anthropomorphic tabby cat dressed in a historical Italian costume against a plain white background. The cat wears a sweeping brown and gold cloak (tabarro), a dark hood framing its feline face, and a long red coat accented with structured button details. In one paw, it holds up a traditional white Carnival mask, while a black tricorn hat (tricorno) is tucked under its arm. Elegant script at the bottom reads "Bauta - Firenze".
history: It features a contemporary artistic rendering that celebrates classic Italian theatrical and festive traditions. The attire depicted is the Bauta, one of the most famous and historically significant disguises of the Venetian Carnival, widely worn during the 17th and 18th centuries. The ensemble was designed specifically to grant total anonymity across social classes, featuring a unique white mask (larva) shaped to let the wearer eat and talk without removing it. While the costume itself is iconic to Venice, the inscription "Firenze" (Florence) indicates its place within a broader regional art collection celebrating the historical pageantry and Commedia dell'Arte heritage of Italy. By Susan Hebert.

title: The New Key by Tube
description: vintage travel poster features a vibrant watercolor illustration dominated by a dense arrangement of colorful red poppies and blue iris flowers in the foreground. In the background, the modern glass and metal structure of the Princess of Wales Conservatory is subtly visible under a pale blue sky. The top border contains bold text reading "The new Kew by Tube" alongside the iconic red and blue London Underground roundel logo.
history: Commissioned by Art on the Underground in 1987, this original poster by British artist Jennie Tuffs was created to promote travel via the London Underground to Kew Gardens. It celebrates the opening of the glass conservatory, keeping with London Transport’s long-standing tradition of hiring prominent artists to advertise leisure travel to the city's green spaces.

title: Houses of Mostar
description: Impressionist-style painting depicts a close-up, low-angle view of old European stone buildings under a deep blue sky. The central structures are rendered in textured strokes, featuring one vibrant magenta building and an adjacent pale purple facade adorned with an antique black streetlamp. The roofs are dark and weathered, and the artist's white stylized signature is visible in the bottom right corner.
history: The artwork captures the essence of traditional Balkan and Mediterranean architecture, heavily reminiscent of historic old towns like Mostar. The combination of centuries-old stone masonry with lively, colorful stucco washes reflects a cultural practice of revitalizing historic urban landscapes. The inclusion of the classic wrought-iron lantern highlights the preservation of romantic, pre-industrial charm in European historic districts.

title: Recipes from Viennese cuisine: Wiener Schnitzel
description: Warm-toned illustration of a Wiener Schnitzel, presenting a large, golden-brown breaded cutlet on a plate garnishing lemon wedges and parsley. Above the plate, a small card reads "taste vienna," and a side dish of potato salad is partially visible in the top left corner. The bottom half of the card contains printed text in German detailing the ingredients and traditional preparation recipe for the dish.
history: The Wiener Schnitzel is a protected national dish of Austria and a culinary symbol of Viennese cuisine. Historically derived from thin, tenderized veal cutlets, its origins are closely tied to the 19th-century refinement of Austrian court cooking, though legends often link it to the Italian Cotoletta alla Milanese. Traditionally, a true Wiener Schnitzel must exclusively use veal, fried to a wavy crisp in clarified butter, and served alongside potato salad or parsley potatoes.

title: Bunny Food - Taiwan Street Food
description: Textured illustration showcasing an array of Taiwanese street food delicacies reimagined with adorable animal faces. In the center, a clear cup of boba milk tea features tapioca pearls shaped like tiny black rabbits. Surrounding the drink are various treats: a wheel cake (imagawayaki) cut open to reveal a sweet red bean filling with eyes, a bag of golden sweet potato balls shaped like bunnies, a piece of crispy Taiwanese fried chicken with a cat-like face, and a glossy, red strawberry tanghulu skewer on the left. The artwork uses warm, grainy textures and soft earth tones.
history: This postcard features the work of ririkoko 梨々子々, an independent Taiwanese digital illustrator known for blending culinary art with animal motifs. The brand name ririkoko is a playful phonetic translation of the Taiwanese Hokkien phrase li-li-khou-khou (哩哩摳摳), which means "many small, miscellaneous things"—reflecting the artist's love for small daily joys and miniature collectibles. By infusing iconic Taiwanese night market treats with a distinct contemporary kawaii (cute) aesthetic, ririkoko's work epitomizes a popular 21st-century movement among young Taiwanese designers who use comforting, whimsical illustrations to celebrate, preserve, and globally export local street food heritage

title: Miho no gen (Shizuoka)
description: Minimalist woodblock print featuring Mount Fuji with its iconic snow-capped peak rising under a clear light-blue sky. In the foreground, vibrant green coastal hills flank a calm blue bay with a sandy curved shoreline stretching across the center. A traditional red square artist seal is stamped in the lower-left corner of the artwork.
history: The postcard captures a classic landscape in the tradition of Shin-hanga or Ukiyo-e woodblock printing, heavily inspired by scenic vistas like the Satta Pass or Miho no Matsubara. Mount Fuji has served as a sacred symbol of longevity, spiritual devotion, and national identity in Japan for centuries, famously popularized worldwide by artists like Katsushika Hokusai. This composition reflects the cultural practice of celebrating Japan's timeless natural beauty by contrasting the permanence of the sacred mountain with the serene, shifting coastal tides.

title: View of Katsuoji Temple
description: Vintage black-and-white photograph showcases an elevated view of a traditional, single-story Japanese wooden pavilion nestled directly beneath a densely forested hillside. Positioned on a massive, tiered stone wall overlooking the structure sits a prominent outdoor stone Buddha statue (Daibutsu) depicted resting in a cross-legged meditative pose on a stone lotus pedestal. Vertical columns of Japanese text run along the right border, contrasting against the light-gray path that frames the right side of the shrine grounds.
history: Historic mountainside grounds of Katsuō-ji, an ancient Buddhist temple founded in 765 AD in Minoh, north of Osaka. Famously designated by imperial courts and powerful samurai clans over the centuries as a sacred site to pray for national safety, its name literally translates to the “Temple of Winning Luck”. The location is globally recognized today for its vibrant cultural tradition where worshippers leave behind thousands of red Daruma dolls across every surface of the mountain complex to symbolize resilience and goals achieved.

title: Zurich 1576, excerpt from Jos Murer's city map
description: Bird's-eye perspective illustration of a medieval European city waterfront executed in an old woodcut print style. The centerpiece of the composition is a prominent stone cathedral with twin, towering pointed spires rising high above dense clusters of half-timbered houses, narrow streets, and fortification towers. In the foreground, a flowing river features small rowing boats, a waterwheel, and wooden docks connected to riverside buildings labeled with German gothic script.
history: Historical view of the Grossmünster, a landmark Romanesque-style Protestant church that dominates the old town skyline of Zurich, Switzerland. According to legend, the church was originally commissioned by Charlemagne after his horse stumbled upon the graves of the city's patron saints, Felix and Regula. It played a monumental role in European history during the 16th century as the starting point of the Swiss-German Reformation led by Huldrych Zwingli.

title: Seagull Method Cafe
description: Two stacked, mirrored groupings of four stylized figures interacting in a interconnected line, rendered entirely in a single, vivid reddish-orange hue against a stark white backdrop. The clean, high-contrast outlines and textured dot patterns on the clothing define the forms, helping individuals with low vision distinguish the quirky, overlapping poses of the characters and the small seagull perched on one of their backs.
history: This custom illustration was created by Ukrainian artist Myroslava Shevchenko (known professionally as Mrsl Va) as part of the visual brand identity for the Seagull Method Cafe, an established brunch destination located in Lisbon, Portugal. The distinctive piece balances playful body language with a maritime motif, encapsulating the slow-paced, communal morning atmosphere that characterizes the city's modern cafe culture.

title: Winter Landscape with Skaters
description: Highly detailed, panoramic oil painting depicting a bustling [winter landscape] beneath a pale, overcast sky filled with soft yellowish light. The composition balances dark bare trees, snow-dusted rustic houses, and beached boats along the left bank with a wide expanse of frozen water on the right, where dozens of tiny figures in contrasting dark garments engage in various ice activities, allowing individuals with low vision to readily distinguish the lively scale of the scene.
history: This famous artwork, titled Winter Landscape with Skaters, was painted around 1608 by the Dutch master Hendrick Avercamp. Currently preserved in the [Rijksmuseum] in Amsterdam, it serves as a premier historical record of everyday life during the Little Ice Age, brilliantly capturing people from all social classes mingling, playing golf-like games, and skating on the ice.

title: Lovely Day for a Guinness
description: Vintage-style advertisement poster for the Irish stout brand Guinness, set against an off-white background with a dark green border. In the center, a cartoon green tortoise walks toward the right, carefully balancing an enormous, full pint glass of dark Guinness beer with a thick, frothy white head on top of its shell. At the top of the poster, the iconic slogan "Lovely day for a GUINNESS" is printed in bold red letters, with "GUINNESS" appearing in a much larger font. At the very bottom, the word "IRELAND" is written in a stylized, historic Celtic-style black font.
history: One of the most famous and enduring advertisement campaigns in brewing history, originally created by the illustrator John Gilroy for the S.H. Benson advertising agency in the 1930s. Gilroy’s iconic zoo animal series—which famously included a tortoise, a toucan, a sea lion, and a kangaroo—revolutionized commercial illustration by injecting humor, vivid color, and whimsical narratives into a brand that had previously relied on more conservative layouts. The turtle balancing a pint was playfully used to represent the slow, meticulous patience required to perfectly pour a pint of Guinness stout, turning a potential consumer drawback into a beloved cultural trademark. Today, these vintage illustrations remain powerful symbols of Irish pub culture, heritage, and international nostalgia.

title: Calçada do Botelho
store: IPOR Livraria Portuguesa e Galeria de Arte
description: Vibrant postcard features a whimsical, watercolor-style illustration of a narrow, steep urban street framed by tall, densely packed apartment buildings with green window frames and hanging laundry. Winding down the center of the asphalt road is a large, serpentine traditional Chinese dragon with golden-orange scales and a red spine. Two stylized cartoonish characters are playfully riding on the dragon's back near its head; one holds a small red banner with Chinese characters. The bright white borders and clean ink linework make the distinctive street signs, local architecture, and playful subjects easy to discern for individuals with low vision.
history: This postcard is created by the popular local Macau brand and independent illustrator Mikel Ko, the creative mind behind the creative platform Finding Mikel 米米插畫. The artwork charmingly depicts Calçada do Botelho (沙欄仔斜路)—a historic winding street in Macau—fusing its distinct Sino-Portuguese urban textures with whimsical folklore. Mikel's signature style blends everyday tourist landscapes with local IP characters to capture and celebrate the vibrant cultural identity of Macanese street life 澳門原創文創品牌－Finding Mikel 米米插畫.

title: Prospect of Rosenborg Castle in the time of Christian VI
description: Depicting the symmetrical facade of Rosenborg Castle in Copenhagen, viewed from an elevated perspective across the expansive King's Garden (Kongens Have). The three-story Dutch Renaissance palace stands centrally with its iconic soaring spires, surrounded by meticulously manicured Baroque hedge gardens, gravel pathways, and small water fountains where figures in 17th- or 18th-century period clothing stroll. Heavy, lush green tree canopies frame the lower foreground, while windmills dot the soft green hills rolling toward the horizon under a pale, cloudy sky.
history: Historic painting—specifically a famous 18th-century gouache projection—capturing Rosenborg Castle and its royal pleasure gardens during its architectural golden age. Built between 1606 and 1634 by King Christian IV as a summer residence, the castle is a prime example of Dutch Renaissance architecture in Scandinavia. The elaborate formal gardens showcased here, originally laid out before the castle itself, reflect the absolute monarchy's transition toward Baroque aesthetic ideals of symmetry and human dominance over nature. As a postcard artifact, this piece highlights Denmark’s deep-seated pride in its royal lineage, preservation of its green urban heritage (Kongens Have remains the oldest royal garden in the country), and classic European landscape art traditions.

title: Tintin au Tibet
description: iconic comic book cover art for "Tintin au Tibet", composed with high-contrast outlines and flat colors against a dominant white background representing a snowy mountain terrain. In the upper center, a large, bold red sun serves as a striking visual anchor, with the title stylized in black cursive text layered inside it. Below, three mountaineering figures—Tintin in blue, Captain Haddock trailing closely behind him with a heavy backpack, and Tharkey leading in a green jacket—trek upwards along a steep ridge, following a clear sequence of large footprints in the snow that curve toward the top right, while the small white dog Snowy runs ahead near a jagged rock formation.
history: This artwork is the classic cover of "Tintin au Tibet" (Tintin in Tibet), the twentieth volume in the world-renowned comic series The Adventures of Tintin, created by the legendary Belgian cartoonist Georges Remi under the pen name Hergé [Tintin in Tibet — Tintin.com]. Initially serialized in 1959, the story is highly regarded by critics as Hergé's masterpiece [Tintin in Tibet — Tintin.com]. It departs from his typical political mysteries to deliver a deeply emotional, character-driven adventure centered on loyalty and Tintin's desperate rescue mission to find his friend Chang in the Himalayas.

title: Longshan Temple
store: CKS Memorial Hall Museum Gift Shop
description: Vintage-style textured illustration depicting the grand frontal facade of a traditional Taiwanese temple against a plain white background. The structure features a striking sweeping orange-tiled roof with dramatic upturned eaves decorated with detailed carvings of dragons and phoenixes. The ornate wooden facade includes gold-accented pillars, hanging red lanterns, and small oval window niches on the sides displaying Buddha statues. In front of the entrance sit two potted bonsai trees and a central bronze incense burner. At the bottom, text in black reads "寺廟 ． 台灣" (Temple ． Taiwan), followed by "Temple" in English and "お寺" in Japanese.
history: The iconic Bangka Longshan Temple in Taipei, Taiwan. Originally built in 1738 by immigrants from Fujian, China, it stands as one of Taiwan's oldest and most architecturally significant spiritual landmarks. The design showcases classical Southern Chinese (Minnan) temple architecture, famous for its swallow-tail ridged roofs and intricate multi-layered woodcarvings. Serving as a multi-denominational hub where Buddhist, Taoist, and folk deities like Mazu are worshipped together, the temple represents the core of Taipei’s community history and religious resilience. Postcards featuring tri-lingual text (Chinese, English, and Japanese) became popular in the mid-to-late 20th century to cater to international heritage tourists.

title: Stamboul
description: Art Deco theatrical poster featuring a dramatic, high-contrast color scheme dominated by a flat, vivid yellow sky. In the right foreground, tall, stylized cypress trees rise in deep green and midnight blue tones, casting elongated shadows across the ground. On the lower left, a lone figure draped in white walks near a silhouetted red-hued cityscape with mosques and minaretes beneath a tiny pink crescent moon. The bottom third of the poster presents a highly legible block of text in bold, uppercase black typography on a solid white background.
history: Original lithographic poster from 1922, created by artist René H. Pesle, was designed to promote the French opera "Stamboul" (Istanbul) [Original Vintage Poster: Stamboul - Eduard Tremisot]. The performance is a lyric drama with poems and music by composer Edouard Trémisot, adapted from Pierre Frondaie's play and the 1900 Orientalist novel L'Homme qui assassina by Claude Farrère [Istanbul Stamboul Edouard Tremisot Art Deco - AntikBar]. The striking visual captures the contemporary Western fascination with the exoticism, mysticism, and historical architecture of old Istanbul

title: Cats Museum of Catarro
description: This postcard showcases a vintage, whimsical illustration centered around a large, expressive black cat surrounded by a dense crowd of smaller black cats against a warm, faded golden and pinkish gradient backdrop. The central cat is depicted sitting forward with an open mouth, wide yellow eyes, and an enthusiastic expression as if laughing or vocalizing. The entire scene is framed by a thin yellow inner border and a thick black outer margin, featuring bold yellow text at the bottom that reads "CATS MUSEUM" above an official website address.
history: This postcard is a souvenir from the specialized Cats Museum (Kotor Cats Museum), a unique cultural institution located in the medieval Old Town of Kotor, Montenegro. The museum's vast archive originates from a significant historical collection donated by an Italian art expert from Venice, containing centuries of feline-themed engravings, antique books, and vintage postcards. A symbolic entry fee is collected from visitors to directly fund and support the care, feeding, and medical needs of Kotor's beloved community of free-roaming street cats

title: Happy Easter!
description: Vintage art postcard features a pastoral, soft-green background decorated with large, overlapping branches of soft, fluffy pussy willow catkins and green birch tassels. Centered on the upper half is a gilded, oval-framed vignette showing a peaceful spring landscape under a blue sky, featuring two prominent white-barked birch trees over a grassy green meadow where a small flock of sheep is grazing. On the top left corner, the greeting text is neatly printed in stylized, capitalized red lettering, offering high legibility for individuals with low vision due to the solid background separation.
history: This vintage greeting card from 1908 features the traditional Latvian greeting "Preezigus Leeldeenas Swehtkus!" (written in modern orthography as Priecīgus Lieldienas svētkus!), which translates to "Happy Easter!" The postcard beautifully reflects Baltic Easter customs, combining the Christian holiday with traditional folklore motifs of the region—such as pussy willows (used in place of palm branches for blessing ceremonies) and birch trees, which symbolize renewal, spring awakening, and the rebirth of nature.

title: Johnston Road
description: vintage photo postcard captures a bustling street scene in a dense Asian metropolis, dominated by a green, double-decker electric tram moving along tracks in the center. The tram is adorned with a prominent black billboard advertising "OLYMPUS" with an illustration of a classic camera. High-rise apartment buildings with crowded balconies and numerous vertical Chinese commercial signs line both sides of the narrow street under a clear blue sky, allowing individuals with low vision to readily distinguish the layered textures, urban density, and nostalgic atmosphere of the transit system.
history: This postcard features a nostalgic shot from the 1980s showcasing a classic double-decker "Ding Ding" streetcar operating on the [Hong Kong Tramways] system, specifically traveling through the vibrant district of Wan Chai along Johnston Road [Hong Kong : 1982]. Serving the northern shore of Hong Kong Island since 1904, these iconic vehicles are a fundamental element of the city's living heritage [A6 Hand-Drawn Postcard : Tram - Paper with Pen]. The scene encapsulates the unique aesthetic of late-20th-century Hong Kong, capturing the juxtaposition of commercial advertisements—such as Olympus and Coca-Cola—with dense urban residential blocks.

title: The Boy and the Heron
description: This postcard reproduces a striking theatrical movie poster featuring a close-up, sketch-style illustration of a mythical avian creature against a stark white background. The artwork uses loose, expressive watercolor textures in shades of deep blue, white, and grey, highlighted by a large, prominent yellow beak and two intense, circular amber eyes looking directly forward. On the lower right, vertical columns of traditional Japanese text are clearly printed in red and black ink, providing a high-contrast layout that allows individuals with low vision to immediately recognize the distinct, iconic character design.
history: This postcard showcases the original teaser poster for "The Boy and the Heron" (Kimi-tachi wa Dō Ikiru ka), the critically acclaimed animated fantasy film written and directed by legendary filmmaker Hayao Miyazaki and produced by Studio Ghibli [The Boy and the Heron - Wikipedia]. Released in 2023, the image became famous worldwide as the sole promotional piece distributed before the movie's Japanese premiere, adhering to an unprecedented silent marketing strategy [The Boy and the Heron - Wikipedia]. The deeply personal story follows a young boy named Mahito who encounters a mysterious grey heron and enters a fantastical world, eventually winning the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature [The Boy and the Heron - Wikipedia].

title: The Kiss
description: highly decorative, iconic painting featuring a couple embracing tightly within an elaborate, shimmering golden shroud against a dark, textured gold background. The man leans over to kiss the woman on the cheek, his robe adorned with sharp, black and white geometric rectangles, while the kneeling woman's gown is decorated with soft, colorful circular flower motifs. They are positioned on a vibrant, grassy meadow densely filled with small, colorful wildflowers, creating a sharp textural contrast that helps individuals with low vision distinguish the central figures from the surrounding metallic space.
history: This world-famous masterpiece, titled "The Kiss" (Der Kuss), was painted between 1907 and 1908 by the prominent Austrian Symbolist painter Gustav Klimt. Considered the high point of his celebrated "Golden Phase," the artwork masterfully incorporates actual gold leaf, silver, and platinum directly into the oil paint to create its radiant, mosaic-like appearance. The original canvas is permanently housed and on public display at the Belvedere Museum in Vienna, Austria, remaining one of the most widely reproduced images of romance and early 20th-century Art Nouveau design.

title: Lisboa
description: textured postcard features an illustrative painting of four street cats interacting around a parked Portuguese police vehicle on a sun-dappled, brownish dirt path. The car, rendered in light cream with distinct blue checkerboard decals and the bold blue word "POLÍCIA" on its side, serves as the central focal point. One cat sits inside looking out the window, another stretches its paws up against the driver's side door, while two others watch from the ground, creating a high-contrast, playful scene easily discernible for individuals with low vision.
history: This artistic print is created by Lisbon-based illustrator Gil B., a popular independent artist recognized for his signature prints sold at the historic Feira da Ladra flea market in Lisbon. The artwork playfully captures the omnipresent street cats of Portugal interacting with a vehicle belonging to the Polícia de Segurança Pública (PSP). Gil B.'s cozy, textured style charmingly juxtaposes public authority symbols with the spontaneous, casual nature of everyday city wildlife.

title: Embankment Place
description: Textured pointillism illustration closely framing the geometric, industrial details of a modern London architectural structure. The composition highlights a cylindrical glass tower with teal-green metal framing and ventilation grilles, contrasted against a massive, white three-dimensional steel truss framework in the background. In the top left corner, the text reads "London's new architecture by bus and tube," accompanied by the iconic red roundel logo of London Transport in the top right.
history: This postcard reproduces a celebrated art poster commissioned by London Transport in 1996, created by the acclaimed printmaker Edwina Ellis. The image is part of a series of intricate multiblock color wood engravings capturing the dramatic rise of postmodern and High-Tech architecture in London. This specific panel depicts a detailed close-up of Embankment Place, the famous complex built over Charing Cross station designed by Terry Farrell. Ellis’s work continues London Transport's world-renowned legacy of employing avant-garde artists to turn public transit marketing into prized pieces of modern graphic design history.

title: Ostrovy, Praha
description: Detailed, outline drawing showcasing a panoramic, bird's-eye view of an urban waterfront landscape. Intricate pen strokes depict dense rows of historic, multi-story European buildings at both the top and bottom edges, framing a wide body of water in the center. The water features small islands covered in rounded, cloud-like trees, a few small boats with figures, and minimal wavy lines to indicate ripples.
history: Illustration by Hungarian artist Balázs Egri captures the distinct architectural identity of Budapest, Hungary, blending elements from the historic sides of Buda and Peste. The crowded, ornate facades reflect the late 19th-century boom of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, a period characterized by Eclectic, Neo-Renaissance, and Art Nouveau styles. By depicting public parks, riverboats, and dense promenades, the artwork celebrates Central Europe's enduring café culture and vibrant urban riverfront life.

title: Macau
description: Highly detailed postcard features a dense, multi-colored architectural collage of Macau's landmarks, unified by bold black ink outlines and a prominent central title in stylized Chinese characters. The composition packs iconic monuments—such as the Macau Tower on the left, the Ruins of St. Paul's at the bottom left, and the Leal Senado building on the right—alongside local culinary delights like an egg tart. The vibrant watercolor tints and clear, rectangular bilingual labels next to each landmark assist individuals with low vision in scanning and identifying the varied historical sites.
history: This postcard is a landmark collage designed by local Macanese illustrator Mikel Ko, the creative force behind the independent brand Finding Mikel 米米插畫. The artwork beautifully interweaves Macau's unique Sino-Portuguese cultural tapestry, showcasing World Heritage architecture alongside traditional snacks and cultural symbols labeled in both Chinese and Portuguese. Mikel's intricate, comic-book-inspired style acts as a visual guide to the territory, celebrating the tight-knit urban density and historical fusion of the region.

title: Genève - Hôtels
description: Art Nouveau style postcard features a structured multi-vignette layout with three stacked oval illustrations framed by an ornate, symmetrical border of deep red and teal blue geometric linework. The top oval captures pedestrians strolling in front of the grand facade of the "Grand Hôtel National." The central oval displays a glowing, yellow-toned sunset over Lake Geneva complete with a sailboat, a steamship, and flying seagulls, while the bottom oval illustrates the historic "Grand Hôtel Métropole" fronted by a large, active fountain. The text headings are crisply printed in bold, dark red and black typography on solid cream bands, creating a highly scannable and accessible design for individuals with low vision.
history: his postcard reproduces a celebrated 1905 Swiss travel lithograph created by Italian-born painter and illustrator Carlo Pellegrini [GENÈVE – HÔTELS - Affiche de Carlo Pellegrini – 1905 – LIGHTMOTIF EDITIONS]. Designed as a joint advertisement for the [Grand Hôtel National] and the [Grand Hôtel Métropole] in Geneva, Switzerland, the artwork brilliantly exemplifies the early 20th-century golden age of tourism promotion [Affiche antiga original Genève, Hôtels National et Métropole]. The elegant vignettes encapsulate the luxurious Belle Époque travel experience, highlighting the city's signature lakeside hospitality, scenic steamship excursions, and iconic architecture.

title: Travessa da Paixão
store: IPOR Livraria Portuguesa e Galeria de Arte
description: This charming, flat-color postcard features a split design showcasing a iconic street scene on the left and a close-up architectural feature on the right, tied together by a bold pink, green, and cream palette. The left section displays a stylized perspective of stacked apartment buildings along a sloping grey street, detailed with pink facades, cream trim, and dark green shuttered doors and windows under a light blue sky [Top 17 Most Instagrammable Places in Macau - Wanderluster Princess]. The right section isolates one of these arched, green shuttered windows [Top 17 Most Instagrammable Places in Macau - Wanderluster Princess] set dramatically against a solid pink background, with clean hand-written text at the bottom of both panels facilitating easy reading for individuals with low vision.
history: This postcard is a custom illustration created by the talented local artist and graphic designer Hio Kuan Lai (黎曉欣). The artwork beautifully captures Travessa da Paixão (commonly known as Love Lane), a picturesque, 50-meter-long historic alleyway in Macau nestled right beside the iconic Ruins of St. Paul's. Her signature clean, illustrative style emphasizes the alley's striking Portuguese-influenced pink facades and classical green windows, adding the playful local question "A Cor do Amor?" (The Color of Love?) to celebrate the street's romantic reputation and its status as a beloved

title: Dragonflies
description: Vintage illustration displays detailed dragonflies, damselflies, and mayflies against a warm ivory background. A wild grass stalk cuts through the center, serving as a perch for a dark-winged damselfly at the top left and an amber-winged female below it. Two large, robust dragonflies dominate the upper right and center, showcasing prominent compound eyes and transparent, amber-veined wings. At the bottom, a brown insect nymph clings to a stem on the left, while two small, delicate mayflies interact on the right, all labeled with tiny scientific numbers.
history: The image is a reprint by the Stockholm design brand Sköna Ting, sourced from a classic British engraving created around 1780 by artist James Newton and naturalist Jacques Barbut. Produced during the Enlightenment, this plate reflects the era's obsession with the Linnaean system, transforming insects from pests into celebrated objects of scientific and artistic beauty. Culturally, the chosen subjects of dragonflies and mayflies served as powerful symbols of transformation and mortality due to their dramatic metamorphosis from underwater nymphs into short-lived, agile aerial predators.

title: Rain or Shine Tiger
store: 來好 LAI HAO 永康本店
description: Vibrant, whimsical illustration features a stylized white tiger covered in bold yellow and black stripes, walking across a bright blue background. Above the tiger are a smiling yellow sun with rays and a grumpy black rain cloud with a sad face, while a small black cat walks beside the tiger's paws and Chinese characters adorn the upper left and bottom right corners.
history: Created by the Hong Kong-based design studio All Things Bright And Beautiful, the artwork's handwritten Chinese calligraphy deeply enriches its visual narrative by introducing profound themes of emotional coexistence and shared resilience. The phrases "有苦，有樂" ("there is bitterness, there is joy") and the Cantonese-inflected "一齊行" ("let's walk this journey together") act as a direct philosophical commentary on the image. By placing these words alongside a whimsical tiger simultaneously bathed in golden sunshine and dynamic rain streaks, the studio masterfully utilizes its signature lighthearted, story-driven artistic style to explore the duality of the human experience. Ultimately, it serves as a comforting reminder of balance and harmony, illustrating that life's hardships and blessings always run parallel, and that navigating these contrasting conditions becomes meaningful through community and companionship.

title: Poster for the Zurich Tourist Office
description: Vintage travel poster features an impressionistic painting of a lively lakeside promenade in Zurich, filled with stylishly dressed pedestrians and docked sailboats. In the background, a steamboat billows smoke under a blue sky, while snow-capped mountains frame the distant horizon above the bold, dark blue "ZURICH" lettering at the bottom.
history: Created in 1916 by the Swiss artist Otto Baumberger, during the early 20th century, this artwork exemplifies the golden age of Swiss travel poster design, which used romanticized, artistic imagery to promote tourism. Posters like this were instrumental in positioning Switzerland—and Zurich specifically—as an accessible, culturally vibrant, and scenic destination for international travelers via expanding rail and steamship networks.

title: Winter Magic in Innsbruck
description: Captures a snowy medieval street in the Altstadt (Old Town) of Innsbruck, Austria. A row of tall pastel-colored buildings with stone arcades and snow-capped bay windows lines the left side, leading the eye to the famous Goldenes Dachl (Golden Roof) balcony with its shimmering, snow-dusted gilded tiles. Thick, falling snowflakes fill the air, blanketing the ground and architectural details while blurry pedestrian silhouettes walk in the background. The German caption at the bottom reads: "Winterzauber in Innsbruck" (Winter Magic in Innsbruck).
history: This image is a contemporary souvenir postcard featuring Innsbruck's most famous landmark, the Golden Roof, completed around 1500 for the Hapsburg Emperor Maximilian I. Built with 2,657 fire-gilded copper tiles, the late-Gothic balcony served as a royal box where the imperial court could watch tournaments and festivals in the square below. Culturally, the postcard celebrates the enduring appeal of the Tyrolean capital, showcasing how its historic alpine architecture harmonizes with winter snowstorms to create the romanticized "winter magic" that has drawn global tourism to the region for generations.

title: Tout sur le chat
description: This educational infographic features a short-haired black cat in side profile, walking across a plain white background [image_5ZbrVk.png]. The cat has bright yellow eyes, pointed ears, and a slightly raised tail [image_5ZbrVk.png]. Multiple pointer lines connect different parts of its body—such as the tail, fur, brain, ears, eyes, nose, body, and paws—to explanatory text blocks written in French that detail feline anatomy and sensory capabilities.
history: This image is from a French visual encyclopedia or science book designed to teach feline biology to a general audience [image_5ZbrVk.png]. The text highlights advanced physiological traits, such as ultrasonic hearing, night vision, and the vomeronasal organ used to detect pheromones [image_5ZbrVk.png]. Historically rooted in 19th-century scientific illustration, this modern infographic reflects the high cultural status of domestic cats in contemporary society by turning everyday curiosity about pet behavior into accessible biological knowledge.

title: Freetown
description: vibrant, expressionistic art print depicts a silhouette cityscape of Freetown Christiania in Copenhagen, Denmark, set against a dramatic, fiery orange and crimson sunset. In the background, the distinctive spiral spire of the Church of Our Saviour rises alongside a red flag bearing three yellow dots, while birds fly across the sky. The foreground features a chaotic, colorful wall covered in graffiti, including a peace sign, a smiley face smoking a cigarette, and words like "FREEDOM" and "RULES SUCK". Two white cats walk along a low green hedge in the center, and a cartoonish rabbit peeks out from the right. The word "FREETOWN" is printed in a bold serif font across the top white border.
history: The artwork was painted by artist Marios Orozco and is distributed as an official print through his Christiania Art Gallery in Copenhagen. Orozco, who has lived and worked inside the autonomous commune since 1981, uses a distinct, heavily textured style to capture the raw aesthetic of his home. Historically, the piece celebrates the counter-cultural identity of this famous enclave, which was established in 1971 by squatters and hippies in an abandoned military barracks. The gritty, rebellious graffiti elements directly reflect Christiania's anti-authoritarian philosophy, its alternative lifestyle ideals, and its legendary open-air cannabis culture.

title: Mostar
description: horizontal art print features a textured, stylized painting of the famous Stari Most (Old Bridge) in Mostar, Bosnia and Herzegovina. The single-arch stone bridge spans a deep blue river, flanked by traditional stone towers and buildings with white-gabled roofs on both banks. On the lower left bank, a row of white cafe umbrellas and brown benches sits along the waterfront. The entire scene is framed by a hazy, deep blue mountain in the background. The word "MOSTAR" is printed in a bold, spaced serif font across the top white border, and "BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA" is written along the bottom.
history: This artwork is a contemporary tourism art print or poster celebrating the city of Mostar, likely created by a local Balkan artist as indicated by the signature and date "20" near the bottom right. The subject is the iconic 16th-century Ottoman bridge, originally commissioned by Suleiman the Magnificent in 1566 and designed by Mimar Hajrudin. Culturally and historically, the bridge is a profound symbol of reconciliation, international cooperation, and cultural diversity. After being destroyed in 1993 during the Bosnian War, its meticulous reconstruction using traditional methods and original local stone came to represent the healing and reunification of a historically divided multicultural community.

title: Tung Choi Street, Mong Kok
description: Watercolor illustration features a wide view of a grand, weathered stone facade set against a clear blue sky, with a sloping green lawn and scattered figures in the foreground. A distinct zigzag path cuts through the lawn, and Chinese characters reading "澳門大三巴" appear in the bottom right corner.
history: This artwork captures the iconic urban landscape and bustling transit system of Hong Kong, specifically highlighting its characteristic red-top public light buses navigating the dense high-rise environment. Such scenes reflect the energetic pace and distinct architectural density that define the city's vibrant street life.

title: Strange Birds / Zhuyin Phonetic Symbols Chart
store: 來好 LAI HAO 永康本店
description: This vertical poster features a phonetic alphabet chart displayed on a clean white background. The chart contains 37 distinct characters arranged in a grid of six rows, with each symbol creatively illustrated as a playful, geometric bird. The primary structural strokes of the characters are rendered in a bold forest green, while quirky anatomical accents like stick legs, wings, and tiny bird heads are highlighted in soft pastel pink. In the upper-left corner, handwritten green text spells out "怪怪鳥" (Strange Birds) above the label "注音符號" (Zhuyin Phonetic Symbols).
history: This print is a modern art postcard designed by Taiwanese illustrator Dong Dong, produced using risograph printing—a vintage mechanical technique celebrated for its vibrant inks and warm, textured imperfections.
